# The Weaver of Dawn

In the time before time, darkness covered all the world. The people huddled in caves, cold and afraid, knowing nothing of light or warmth.

High in the mountains lived an old woman named Ayla, who spent her days weaving at her loom. Her fingers were gnarled like ancient roots, but they moved with practiced grace across the threads. Each day she wove, and each night she unraveled her work, for she had not yet found the pattern she sought.

One morning, a golden spider descended from the ceiling and whispered, "Grandmother, why do you weave and unweave endlessly?"

"I search for the thread that will bring light to the world," Ayla replied.

The spider climbed onto her loom and spun a single strand of silk that shimmered like starlight. "Weave this into your pattern," it said.

Ayla wove the golden thread into her tapestry, and as she worked, the fabric began to glow. Brighter and brighter it shone, until she completed the final stitch. The tapestry burst into brilliant flame and rose into the sky, becoming the first sun.

From that day forward, dawn has returned each morning, following the pattern Ayla wove into the fabric of the world.

# The Tale of the First Echo

Long ago, when the world was newly formed, Sound was a lonely spirit who wandered the earth seeking companionship. She would sing beautiful melodies, but they would drift away into nothingness, never to return.

One day, Sound came upon a deep canyon carved by the ancient rivers. Exhausted from her travels, she sat at its edge and sang a melancholy song about her solitude. To her amazement, the canyon sang back to her—the same melody, slightly softer, but unmistakably her own voice.

Overjoyed, Sound sang again, and again the canyon replied. She had finally found a friend who would listen and respond. She sang louder and louder, and the canyon faithfully returned each note.

But Sound grew greedy. She wanted her companion to sing something new, to create its own melodies. When the canyon only repeated her songs, she became angry and stopped visiting.

The canyon waited in silence, heartbroken.

Eventually, Sound realized her mistake. A true friend doesn't need to be different from you—sometimes the greatest gift is simply being heard and understood.

She returned to the canyon, and they sing together still. That is why, when you call out into the emptiness, the Echo always answers back.
